title: Pear and chocolate strudel
subtitle: filo pastry wrapped around a filling of poached pear, dark chocolate, and almonds
excerpt: Pear and chocolate strudel is a long roll of filo pastry filled with sliced poached pear, dark chocolate chips, and ground almonds, baked until the filo is golden and shattering. The pears soften further inside the parcel as it bakes, and the chocolate melts into the filling. Serve warm with cream or creme fraiche.
sourceNotes: Strudel is most closely associated with the Austro-Hungarian tradition, where apple strudel has been made since at least the eighteenth century. The use of filo pastry as a shortcut to traditional hand-stretched strudel dough has been standard in British home baking since the 1980s. Pear and chocolate as a filling is a contemporary variation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 3 hours ahead, cover with cling film, and refrigerate. Brush with butter and bake straight from the fridge.

content.text: Pear and chocolate strudel is a roll of layered filo pastry enclosing a filling of sliced pear, dark chocolate, and ground almonds. The filo is layered with melted butter between each sheet to give it richness and help the layers separate and crisp in the oven. Filo dries quickly: keep the unused sheets covered with a damp cloth while you work.
Heat the oven to 190 degrees C (fan 170 degrees C / gas 5). Line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Toss the sliced pears with the caster sugar, cinnamon, and chopped chocolate. Mix the ground almonds and breadcrumbs together in a small bowl.
Lay one filo sheet on a large piece of baking paper on the work surface. Brush all over with melted butter. Lay the next sheet on top, brush again, and continue until all sheets are layered.
Scatter the almond and breadcrumb mixture over the filo leaving a 5 cm border all around. Mound the pear and chocolate filling along one long edge, again leaving a 5 cm border at the ends.

Fold the short edges of the filo over the filling, then roll up along the long edge, using the baking paper to help lift and roll. Place seam-side down on the lined tray. Brush all over with the remaining melted butter.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Leave for 10 minutes, then dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

attrs.problem: Filo tearing and falling apart as you roll
attrs.avoid: Avoid letting the filo dry out; it becomes brittle within minutes of being exposed to air.
attrs.fix: Keep unused sheets covered with a lightly damp tea towel. Work quickly and brush each sheet generously with butter as you lay it down.

attrs.problem: Soggy bottom filo layer under the filling
attrs.avoid: Avoid very juicy or ripe pears that release a lot of liquid during baking.
attrs.fix: The breadcrumb and almond layer between the filo and the filling absorbs excess moisture. Pat the sliced pears dry before using if they seem very wet.
